      what the reading said it is: This is a monthly self-inspection checklist designed to track compliance with workplace safety, air quality, fire safety, and chemical handling standards. The company completes this form to verify that key controls are in place each month — air permit posted and valid, scrubber pressure-drop readings logged within operating ranges, detector-tube checks performed, equipment inspections done, fire extinguishers current, exits clear, eyewash and safety showers functional, and safety data sheets available. Any item marked 'N' must be reported to the Plant Manager by the 5th of the following month.
      WHAT THE READING FOUND WRONG WITH IT (8) — these are already findings; carry them, do not re-find them:
        · No document date or completion record visible
            The template shows blanks for Month, Completed by, and Supervisor with no dates or initials filled in. Without a completed instance of this form, it is not possible to verify whether the company is performing these checks or how recent the most recent check was.
            what it needs: Obtain a completed monthly self-check form showing the month reviewed, the date of supervisor review, the employee who completed it, and the results (Y/N and initials) for each line item. Confirm the company fills this out every month.
            the rule: OSHA General Duty Clause (OSH Act Section 5(a)(1)); OAR 340-216-8010 et seq. (Oregon air permit posting and availability requirements)
        · No procedure for tracking or escalating failures  [worked out from the document, not stated in it]
            The form states 'Items marked N are reported to the Plant Manager by the 5th of the following month' but does not specify what happens next — no procedure for investigation, root cause, corrective action, documentation, or verification that issues are fixed before the next month.
            what it needs: Establish a written procedure defining: (1) what constitutes an 'N' result, (2) who investigates, (3) required corrective actions by category, (4) documentation requirements, (5) verification that fixes are in place before the next check, (6) escalation criteria for repeated failures or safety risks.
            the rule: OSHA General Duty Clause; 29 CFR 1910.22 (general safety requirements); Oregon DEQ permit conditions typically require prompt correction of deficiencies
        · Missing scope for Line 3 — C-1 detector-tube check frequency and method  [worked out from the document, not stated in it]
            Line 3 calls for 'Weekly C-1 detector-tube checks done and recorded every week this month' but the checklist does not specify what constitutes a valid check (e.g., testing method, recording format, pass/fail criteria, action if outlet exceeds threshold).
            what it needs: Add to the procedure or attach a reference document: the standard or protocol for C-1 outlet detector-tube testing, the acceptable range or pass criterion, the required log format, and what corrective action is required if the check shows a failure.
            the rule: Oregon air permit conditions for scrubber outlet monitoring (likely specified in Permit 26-2841-ST-01 or its attachments); ANSI/ASABE standard or equivalent
        · Missing acceptance range for Line 2 — scrubber pressure-drop readings
            Line 2 specifies 'readings between 2.0 and 6.0' but does not clarify the units (inches water column, bar, kPa, etc.) or reference the source permit condition that sets this range.
            what it needs: Amend Line 2 to state the units of measurement (e.g., 'readings between 2.0 and 6.0 inches of water column') and add a reference to the permit condition or design document that establishes this range.
            the rule: Oregon air permit conditions for scrubber operations; company's own Scrubber Pressure-Drop Log document already exists
        · No definition of defect follow-up documentation for Line 4  [worked out from the document, not stated in it]
            Line 4 requires 'any defect followed up' but does not specify what follow-up means — repair timelines, work orders, log entries, supervisor approval, or sign-off required.
            what it needs: Add to the procedure or manual: define 'follow-up' to include (1) creation of work order or incident report, (2) severity/urgency category, (3) repair deadline (e.g., before next use, within 24 hours, within one week), (4) required documentation (photos, maintenance log entry, mechanic's sign-off), and (5) verification that defect was corrected before the truck next runs.
            the rule: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178 (powered industrial truck operation and maintenance); company's own PIT Pre-Shift Inspection Log already documents daily checks
        · Fire extinguisher tag protocol not specified  [worked out from the document, not stated in it]
            Line 5 states fire extinguishers must be 'tagged within the last 12 months; monthly visual check initialled on each tag' but does not specify who performs the monthly check (technician or any employee), where initials go, or what visual checks constitute pass/fail.
            what it needs: Add procedures for fire extinguisher maintenance: (1) annual professional inspection/recharge must be performed by a certified service company; (2) monthly visual walk-through: check for damage, blockage, pressure gauge in green zone; (3) log and initial a tag on the extinguisher or maintain a separate log; (4) any defect triggers immediate service or replacement. Reference NFPA 10 or equivalent.
            the rule: NFPA 10 (Standard for Portable Fire Extinguishers); OSHA 29 CFR 1910.157 (general requirements for all portable fire extinguishers)
        · Eyewash and safety shower flush protocol incomplete  [worked out from the document, not stated in it]
            Line 7 calls for 'Eyewash stations and safety showers flushed this week and logged' but does not specify duration of flush, acceptance criteria, or where logs are kept.
            what it needs: Add to the procedure: (1) flushing frequency (at minimum weekly; some standards require daily or when in use); (2) flush duration (typically 1–3 minutes to clear lines); (3) visual inspection for water flow, clarity, and nozzle function; (4) log entry must include date, time, location, flush duration, any defects noted, and initials; (5) any malfunction must trigger repair/replacement before next work day.
            the rule: ANSI Z535.4 (labeling and marking of hazardous substances); OSHA 29 CFR 1910.151 (eye and face protection); many states and facilities follow ANSI Z535.1 or local code for emergency equipment inspection
        · SDS binder update protocol undefined  [worked out from the document, not stated in it]
            Line 8 requires 'Safety data sheets on hand for every chemical received this month; binder index updated' but does not define who updates the index, how indexing is organized, or how obsolete SDSs are removed.
            what it needs: Add to the SDS management procedure: (1) designate responsible person(s); (2) require SDS to be obtained and added to binder within X days of receipt (commonly within 5–10 days); (3) organize by product name, CAS number, or hazard category with consistent labeling; (4) maintain an index or log with product name, receipt date, SDS version date, and location in binder; (5) remove and archive obsolete SDSs (keep for X years per record retention policy); (6) verify accessibility during inspections; (7) train all employees on binder location and use.
            the rule: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(g) (Hazard Communication Standard, SDS requirements)
      DATES THIS DOCUMENT SETS (1):
        · Items marked N reported to Plant Manager — no date stated (recurring)
      WHAT THE READING SAID A COMPANY LIKE THIS USUALLY ALSO HOLDS (7) —
        a suggestion from similar companies, NOT a checked requirement:
        · Completed monthly forms for prior months — To verify the company is actually conducting these checks monthly and responding to failures, a history of completed forms is essential. Without them, the template is a procedure document only, not evidence of compliance.
        · Escalation or investigation log for 'N' results — The checklist states failures go to the Plant Manager by the 5th of the following month, but no log of those reports, investigations, or remediation actions was provided. This is critical evidence that problems are addressed.
        · Exit route and emergency egress audit or floor plan — Line 6 checks that exits and aisles are clear and signs are lit, but no floor plan, exit signage documentation, or periodic egress audit procedure is provided.
        · Fire extinguisher maintenance contract or service record — Line 5 requires annual professional tagging and monthly checks. The company should hold a service contract and annual maintenance records, which are missing from the submission.
        · Powered Industrial Truck operator training and evaluation records — The company has a 'Powered Industrial Truck Operator Training and Evaluation Record' in its document list, but how that links to the pre-shift inspection protocol on Line 4 is not shown.
        · Scrubber maintenance and testing SOP — Line 2 and 3 reference specific monitoring ranges and detector-tube checks, but the actual procedure, acceptance criteria, and corrective-action thresholds are not attached or incorporated.
        · SDS master list or binder with current index — Line 8 requires an updated SDS binder and index. The template does not show how many chemicals are in inventory or what the current index looks like.

            the rule: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7)
        · No supervisor review signature or date
            The log form has a line for 'Supervisor review' with blanks for signature and date, but both are left blank and unsigned. This undermines accountability and verification of the log's completeness.
            what it needs: Have a supervisor sign and date the log to certify that they have reviewed the inspections and that all required entries have been completed.
            the rule: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) (requires documented examination); Oregon Administrative Rules OAR 437-004-1178(q)(7) (likely mirrors federal standard)
        · Defect not resolved—horn not working on September 9
            On 9 September, the horn was marked with an X (defect) with the note 'Horn not working'. The log shows the truck continued to be used on subsequent days, but there is no record of when the horn was repaired or whether a work order was issued. findings.quote: The permittee shall submit a complete application for renewal of this permit no later than 120 days before the expiration date, that is, on or before July 18, 2026
findings.what_to_do: Nothing if renewal application was timely submitted. If not submitted by July 18, 2026, document this failure immediately and file renewal application now to avoid lapse in permit coverage.

findings.title: Monthly self-check forms completion and record
findings.quote: The template shows blanks for Month, Completed by, and Supervisor with no dates or initials filled in. Without a completed instance of this form, it is not possible to verify whether the company is performing these checks or how recent the most recent check was.
findings.what_to_do: Produce completed monthly self-check forms for each month from the program's inception through the present. For each form, confirm the month, date of completion, employee who completed it, supervisor who reviewed it with date, and results (Y/N with initials) for all eight line items. Upload to file or produce for inspector.

findings.title: Escalation and corrective-action procedure for failed self-check items
findings.what_to_do: The inspector will ask: when a self-check item is marked 'N', what investigation occurs, who does it, how is it documented, and how is resolution verified before the next month? The template states items go to the Plant Manager by the 5th but provides no procedure for investigation, root cause, corrective action, or verification. Prepare to explain the process by which you receive the failed item, investigate it, determine the fix, document the fix, and verify it is in place before the next check.

findings.title: Detector-tube check protocol and acceptance criteria
findings.what_to_do: The inspector will ask: what is the standard method for a C-1 detector-tube check? What is the pass/fail threshold? What do you do if a check shows breakthrough? The self-check form calls for 'Weekly C-1 detector-tube checks done and recorded every week this month' but does not define the method, acceptance range, or corrective action. Prepare to describe the test procedure, the outlet concentration threshold your permit requires, and what happens if you detect breakthrough.

findings.title: Scrubber pressure-drop units of measurement
findings.what_to_do: Amend the self-check form Line 2 to state the units: 'readings between 2.0 and 6.0 inches of water column' to match the permit language and eliminate ambiguity. Update form and upload to file.

findings.title: Equipment defect follow-up documentation procedure
findings.what_to_do: The inspector will ask: when a defect is found during a self-check, how and when must it be reported, and how long do you have to fix it? The form says 'any defect followed up' but does not define follow-up. Prepare to explain the process: for example, who creates a work order, what is the repair deadline (e.g., before next use, within 24 hours), what documentation is required, and how is completion verified.

findings.title: Fire extinguisher monthly check protocol and documentation
findings.what_to_do: The inspector will ask: who performs the monthly visual checks on fire extinguishers, where is that recorded, and how do you verify the pressure is in the green zone? The form states 'monthly visual check initialled on each tag' but does not specify the check method or what pass/fail means. Prepare to describe: which employee does the monthly walk-around, what they check for (pressure, damage, blockage, obstruction), where they initial (on tag or log), and what happens if a defect is found.

findings.title: Fire extinguisher annual maintenance records
findings.what_to_do: Produce fire extinguisher annual maintenance and recharge records. The self-check requires fire extinguishers to be 'tagged within the last 12 months' but the company holds only a title for 'Certificate of Annual Maintenance — Portable Fire Extinguishers' dated 2025-08-20. Upload the contents of that certificate or produce the maintenance contracts and service records from the certified service provider showing annual inspection, recharge, and tag dates for all extinguishers on site.

findings.title: Eyewash station and safety shower flushing records
findings.what_to_do: Produce flushing logs for eyewash stations and safety showers. The self-check requires 'Eyewash stations and safety showers flushed this week and logged' but no logs were produced. Obtain or create a flushing log for each station showing date, time, duration of flush, visual inspection results (water flow, nozzle function), any defects noted, and operator initials. Submit logs for at least the past 12 months.

findings.title: Safety Data Sheet binder and index
findings.what_to_do: Produce the SDS binder with current index. The self-check requires 'Safety data sheets on hand for every chemical received this month; binder index updated' but the binder and index were not produced. The company holds one SDS title ('Safety Data Sheet - Sodium Hydroxide Solution, 50%' dated 2024-03-18) but the complete binder with index is missing. Upload a current index listing all chemicals in use, SDS receipt date, SDS version date, and location in binder. Confirm all chemicals in use have current SDSs in the binder and accessible to employees.

findings.title: Powered Industrial Truck pre-shift inspection gaps — September 3–6
findings.locator: Page 1-2, inspection log table and note
findings.quote: The hour meter shows the truck ran on 5-6 September (hours increased from 4,819 at Sep 2 to 4,834 at Sep 7), but no inspections are documented for Sep 3, 4, 5, or 6.
findings.what_to_do: Produce pre-shift inspection records for September 3, 4, 5, and 6, 2026. If inspections were performed but not recorded, complete the missing entries now showing date, operator, inspection results for all 12 checklist items, hours logged, and operator initials. If the truck was not operated those days, correct the hour meter record to show accurate equipment hours.

findings.title: Powered Industrial Truck pre-shift inspection — supervisor review signature
findings.quote: The log form has a line for 'Supervisor review' with blanks for signature and date, but both are left blank and unsigned.
findings.what_to_do: Have the warehouse supervisor (or designee) review the completed September 2026 pre-shift inspection log, verify all entries are complete and accurate, and sign and date the supervisor review line immediately.

findings.title: Powered Industrial Truck horn defect — September 9 — unresolved
findings.locator: Page 2, September 9 row, horn column marked X with note 'Horn not working'
findings.quote: On 9 September, the horn was marked with an X (defect) with the note 'Horn not working'. The log shows the truck continued to be used on subsequent days, but there is no record of when the horn was repaired or whether a work order was issued.
findings.what_to_do: Produce a maintenance work order, repair record, or mechanic's log showing the date the horn defect was reported, the date and time of repair, the method of repair or replacement, and verification that the horn was tested and working before the truck was placed back in service. If the truck was used after September 9 with a defective horn, document why this was permitted.

findings.title: Scrubber pressure-drop log — missing supervisor sign-off
findings.locator: Page 1 (August) and Page 2 (September), supervisor review signature line
findings.quote: Both August and September logs show blank lines for supervisor review signature and date, which are required for record completion and permit compliance.
findings.what_to_do: Have the facility supervisor review and sign the August 2026 and September 2026 scrubber pressure-drop logs with date on both pages immediately.

findings.title: Carbon adsorption unit C-1 detector-tube checks — September incomplete
findings.quote: The September detector-tube log shows only two entries (Sep 7 and Sep 21) when the condition requires weekly checks. September has five weeks and should have five weekly readings recorded.
findings.what_to_do: Add missing weekly C-1 detector-tube check readings for September 14 and September 28 (or provide documentation showing which weeks in September corresponded to the required five weekly checks). Record the date, time, tube reading in ppm, whether breakthrough was detected, and name of person performing the check.

findings.title: Scrubber S-2 pressure-drop exceedance — September 9
findings.what_to_do: Document the cause of the September 9 pressure-drop exceedance on the caustic line (S-2 recorded 6.4 inches of water column, exceeding the 6.0-inch maximum). Provide an explanation and corrective action taken (e.g., nozzle inspection or cleaning, line blockage cleared, gauge recalibrated). Determine whether permit Condition 5.2 required notification to Oregon DEQ within 24 hours and, if so, produce the notification or explain why it was not required.

findings.title: Annual report submission for 2025
findings.what_to_do: Nothing. Annual report for 2025 is on file dated February 10, 2026, within the February 15 deadline required by the permit.

findings.title: Annual report submission deadline for 2026
findings.what_to_do: Prepare the 2026 annual report for submission to Oregon DEQ by February 15, 2027. Report must cover calendar year 2026 operations including throughput by line, scrubber pressure-drop summaries, carbon replacement dates, quarterly scrubber inspection records, and any deviation or excess emission events.

findings.title: Semi-annual monitoring report submission — January–June 2026
findings.what_to_do: Produce the semi-annual monitoring report for the reporting period January 1–June 30, 2026, or confirm it was submitted to Oregon DEQ by July 31, 2026 deadline. If not submitted, file it now and notify DEQ that it was late. The report must document operations for the first six months of 2026.

findings.title: Carbon replacement for C-1 — scheduled replacement March 14, 2026
findings.quote: The carbon in C-1 was replaced on March 14, 2025 (Calgon Filtrasorb 400, 1,800 pounds, by Northwest Carbon Services). The next scheduled replacement is on or before March 14, 2026.
findings.what_to_do: Produce documentation that the C-1 carbon was replaced on or before March 14, 2026. The 2025 annual report scheduled replacement for March 14, 2026 (one year after the March 14, 2025 replacement). Provide receipt, invoice, or work order showing date of replacement, carbon type and weight, and vendor name. If replacement did not occur by March 14, 2026, provide the weekly detector-tube check records for the weeks after that date showing no breakthrough was detected.

findings.title: Deviation report — August 22 pump failure (DEV-2025-0913)
findings.locator: Page 3, Section 5 mentions deviation but full report not included
findings.what_to_do: Produce the written deviation report for the August 22 pump failure referenced in the 2025 annual report as 'DEV-2025-0913'. The report must be dated within 15 days of discovery and describe the deviation, cause, duration, and corrective action taken. Confirm it was submitted to Oregon DEQ within the 15-day window and produce a copy of the submission or DEQ receipt.

findings.title: Quarterly scrubber inspection records — supporting documentation
findings.locator: Page 3, Section 3 references 'mentioned as existing in scrubber maintenance file'
findings.what_to_do: Produce quarterly scrubber maintenance inspection records for scrubbers S-1 and S-2. The 2025 annual report references these records but does not include them. The permit requires at least quarterly inspection of pump, nozzles, packing, and mist eliminator for each scrubber. Provide records for all four quarters of 2025 (and through September 2026 for current compliance) showing inspection date, inspector name, components checked, condition, and any corrective actions taken.

findings.title: Daily scrubber pressure-drop logs — supporting detail
findings.locator: Page 2, Section 2 provides summary statistics only
findings.what_to_do: Produce daily scrubber pressure-drop logs for 2025. The 2025 annual report includes only summary statistics (e.g., 'S-1 average 3.8 in. w.c., S-2 average 4.1 in. w.c.') but the permit requires daily logged readings. Upload the underlying daily logs for January 1–December 31, 2025, showing date, scrubber operating status, and pressure-drop readings for each day the scrubber was in operation.

findings.title: Compliance Inspection Checklist — completed form
findings.what_to_do: The checklist is a template used during inspection. Nothing is required from you at this time.
